name: ZeroTier
aliases: zerotier free as a storage mesh

egress.terms: signalling; peer-to-peer once connected, with a relay fallback whose rate is not published

record.chaining: signalling for a small private mesh; it composes with a private set of devices and carries no bytes once they connect.
record.reliability_note: the free plan caps devices, not bytes

evidence.proved: 10 devices, 1 network and 1 admin on the free plan
'ZeroTier enables private networking between devices, allowing you to host a website locally and serve it securely to peers on the same ZeroTier network.'

record.notes: 2026-10-23: no public ingress, in the vendor's own words. The hosting guide says ZeroTier 'enables private networking between devices, allowing you to host a website locally and serve it securely to peers on the same ZeroTier network'. Its UDP 9993 listener is for peer transport, not for a reader, so the free plan's cap on devices is the only meter and there is no 1 TiB/month to spend.

extras.transit_note: peer-to-peer once connected, with a relay fallback at an unpublished rate

record.limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 10 devices on the free plan

card.summary: 10 devices, 1 network. Vendor table effective 20 Oct 2026: 'Personal | Free | 10 | Not available'.

free_tier.stated: 10 devices, 1 network. Vendor table effective 20 Oct 2026: 'Personal | Free | 10 | Not available'.

egress.terms: free, peer-to-peer; relaying only when the path fails.

record.interface_detail: virtual L2/L3 overlay, REST API, Terraform provider, CLI.
record.tooling: zerotier-one agent; central controller is now separately licensed (the default `make` build no longer includes it).
record.chaining: 10 devices is workable as a private mesh but not as a shard farm, and the controller is no longer in the open-source build by default.
record.limits_note: device count, not bandwidth. Data flows peer-to-peer so there is no byte meter.
record.reliability_note: Free tier has been cut twice (50 -> 25 -> 10 devices). Docs at docs.zerotier.com/start/ still say 'up to 25 devices' while the vendor's own llms-full.txt says 10. Trust the vendor table, not the docs page.
